answer: Each agent may submit work, but rewards are released only after a randomly selected peer verifies the result and stakes a deposit that is forfeited if the review proves dishonest. Splitting one identity into a hundred sybils does not multiply influence: each claim still needs an independent, accountable reviewer, and coordinated reviews risk losing the reviewers’ deposits. The attacker must therefore lock up capital and recruit or control credible reviewers, making a fake swarm costly even when identities are cheap. A nectar forecast, comet route, or walnut harvest can all use the same rule.
